turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Hey, come on back. I'm gonna grab a blood pressure and a pulse real quick before Dr. Shah. Is the baby with your partner out front?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, um, my partner has him in the stroller, he's six weeks today, and I almost didn't come because I hate leaving him, but my partner said I had to, I've been a mess, sorry the waiting room was so loud I already feel wound up.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): You're okay. Blood pressure is 118 over 74, pulse 88, oxygen sat 99 percent.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay good. Right after the delivery they kept saying it was one-forty over ninety and rechecking me, so this feels more like me, I think, I hope I'm not talking too much.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): That was then, this is today. He does look pretty anxious out there, pacing. Doctor will be right in, computer's been slow all morning.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ugh, sorry, this thing just logged me out. Uh, what brings you in? I didn't really see the note.

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't sleep. Even when the baby is asleep I just lie there awake, and I cry over everything, the laundry, a commercial, and it's not brand new but it's not the very first days either, those were just visitors and casseroles.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen jumped. Say the main thing one more time?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): The main thing is I cannot sleep even when he's sleeping, and I'm tearful all day. And my head is fine, no headaches or anything, and the stitches from the second-degree tear feel okay, I'm not in pain.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right. How long has the not sleeping been going on? I need something for this field.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm I can't pin the day down. It wasn't that first week. Maybe it crept in around week two, or week three, so that's like four weeks or five, it all runs together when you're up at night, I'm sorry that's not a clean answer.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mm. And the crying, how often?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Every single day, sometimes three or four times, and I can't stop once it starts. I feel so down and flat, and then guilty, because he's actually a good baby, he only wakes twice, and my partner does the two a.m. bottle so I should be sleeping and I'm just not.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No fever. I keep worrying about infection in the stitches so I pay attention, and I don't feel hot, our thermometer is cheap but there's been no fever.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about your stomach, any nausea, vomiting, diarrhea?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No, none of that. Stomach's been fine. I'm eating toast and whatever pasta my partner makes, enough, I think.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough? You got a cough?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh not really a cough. I clear my throat a lot, especially at night, but I wouldn't call it a cough, it's hard to say, the heat in the apartment is so dry.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a message popped up. What was that about the cough, repeat it?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I said it's not a real cough, just a lot of throat clearing at night, and I don't know if that even counts, we keep saying we'll buy a humidifier and we never do.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Okay. I have to ask you straight. Any thoughts of hurting yourself?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Absolutely not. Even when I'm crying I'm not thinking about ending anything, I think about my partner and the baby needing me, I would never.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): And any thoughts of harming the baby?

[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): God, no. It makes me feel sick that you have to ask, but no. I check on him like every ten minutes when he's asleep because I'm scared something will happen to him, not because I would do it. I rearrange his blanket over and over.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, and I need to correct myself, I said my head was fine and that was wrong. When I've been up all night I get this pounding in both temples. It started about last week. If I lie down in a dark room it eases off.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Pounding, both temples. Say that again, I was clicking the wrong tab.

[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Both temples, a pounding headache after nights with no sleep, since about last week, and the dark quiet helps. It's not a migraine, no lights, no throwing up. My mom gets real migraines, I don't.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mom, migraines, okay. Let me just look at that tear.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): It looks healed. No redness, no opening. And you are tearful, I can see it from here.

[SEG0031] person_4 (NURSE): Knock knock, dropping that growth chart you asked for, it's the baby's. My sister was the same way after her second, could not sleep even when the baby slept, she bought blackout curtains for her own bedroom. Not advice, just, yeah, my sister.

[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thanks. So what's going on in the body is, after delivery the estrogen and progesterone drop fast, and if you're not sleeping on top of that the mood pathways get kind of flooded. That's the mechanism. It's not you failing at this.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): My read, and this is provisional, is postpartum depression rather than just baby blues, because you're six weeks out and still this low. I'm not putting a final stamp on it today.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. Um, medicines, since you'll ask or the computer will, I still take my prenatal every morning, that huge pill. For the cramps I take ibuprofin, I thought the bottle was 800 but I looked and it's 600 milligrams, one tablet by mouth when the cramps hit, maybe every other day. And the iron, ferrous sulfate, I stopped, I ran out about two weeks ago and never refilled it.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wait, the iron, say that part again, I was in the med list.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Ferrous sulfate, once a day, and then I stopped when I ran out, about two weeks ago. I don't remember the milligrams, the bottle is on the fridge at home.

[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): And the cramps, I know I said I wasn't in pain, but there is this dull ache low in my belly some evenings. It's not bad. The ibuprofin does help it. The stitches themselves don't hurt.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dull ache, noted. I'm not starting a new medicine today. Try to sleep when he sleeps, even twenty minutes, and let your partner keep that night bottle. I want you back in one week, booked, not a maybe. Front desk can also put you in the postpartum support group.

[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): One week, yes. Can I bring the baby, because my partner works some days and my mom is in Dayton so she's not always around, and I overthink the car seat click, sorry, I do this, I explain too much.
[SEG0040] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I can book both before you go. Thursday morning, nine thirty, for the visit, and I'll add the support group roster. That work?

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thursday at nine thirty works. If any thought of hurting yourself or the baby shows up before then, that's an emergency, go to the ER, don't wait for Thursday. Otherwise I'll see you then.

spec.situation: Mother six weeks after delivery, tearful, not sleeping even when the baby sleeps; partner present and anxious; denies harming herself or the baby when asked directly; support and follow-up planned.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Second-degree tear is supported, but repair and exact 6-weeks-ago timing are not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Perineal tear repair (timeframe=6 weeks ago, reported_by=patient)

bad.reason: Daily tearfulness three or four times supported; 'severe' is not stated.
bad.text: Tearfulness (category=psychiatric, status=present, severity=severe, frequency=every day, three or four times, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Negative finding: no headaches initially reported before later correction ('my head is fine, no headaches or anything').
Negative findings asked and answered: no nausea, no vomiting, and no diarrhea were individually denied.
Negative finding asked and answered: patient denied a real cough ('not a real cough').
Headache associated negatives/details missing: patient said it was not a migraine, with no photophobia ('no lights') and no vomiting.
Medication detail missing for ferrous sulfate: patient had been taking it once daily and stopped because she ran out about two weeks ago and did not refill it.

Symptom detail missing/wrongly generalized: patient said the stitches themselves do not hurt, but she does have a dull low-belly ache some evenings; this was described as an ache rather than 'cramps'.
Plan detail missing: doctor explicitly said no new medicine would be started today.
Follow-up timing detail missing/wrongly recorded: doctor wanted return in one week, booked and not optional; Thursday at 9:30 was the scheduled appointment.
